en.title: Maximum Shipment Batches with Distinct Categories and Increasing Sizes
en.description:
Each category has inventory[i] items. Each batch uses at most one item per category, and each batch must contain strictly more items than the previous one; each item can be used at most once, and leftovers are allowed. Find the maximum number of batches.

The standard I/O, examples and editorial were written independently by this site; ranges explicitly marked as this site's are not the source's original constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n; the second line contains the inventories. The original text had no numeric bounds; this site uses 1≤n≤200000, 0≤inventory[i]≤10^9.
en.output: Output a single integer, the answer.
en.explanation: The answers are 4, 2 and 0. Even with a large total, the two of the three categories that have only one item each cannot both supply the second and the third batches.
hints: Accumulate the inventories in ascending order while maintaining the number of batches k that can be built; each time a new category is included, if the total reaches (k+1)(k+2)/2, increase k by 1. Each category adds at most one batch.
